idea-plugin.name: Maven Detective
idea-plugin.description:
Explains why a Maven build fails – in plain language, with evidence and a quick fix.

  • Build Doctor: instead of 500 lines of log, a card with cause, evidence, confidence and one-click fix.
  • Detects, among others, cached failed downloads (.lastUpdated), missing credentials in settings.xml, blocked http repositories, corrupt JARs, wrong JDK, missing modules and parent POMs.
  • What changed? Every green run becomes the reference; when a later one fails, the card lists the changes since then – JDK, Maven, profiles, parent, plugins, dependencies.
  • IDE vs. command line: compares Maven, JDK, settings.xml, profiles and .mvn/ configuration between IntelliJ and ./mvnw.
  • Why this version? Right-click a dependency in pom.xml to see the decision chain: direct declaration, dependencyManagement in the module or parent, imported BOM, the property that sets it, path in the tree (nearest wins) and overridden versions – every step jumps to the right POM line.
  • Conflict matrix: one table for the whole reactor – artifact by module, resolved version in each cell, deviations highlighted. One click pins the version in the common parent's dependencyManagement and lists the declarations that would still override it.
  • Exclusion hygiene: an inspection in pom.xml greys out exclusions that no longer exclude anything (typically after an upgrade) or that another exclusion already covers; quick fix removes them.
  • Duplicate classes: finds classes that sit in more than one JAR of a module, also under different coordinates (commons-logging next to jcl-over-slf4j, javax.xml.bind next to jakarta.xml.bind-api 2.x), shows which copy wins and whether the contents differ, and inserts the exclusion that removes the redundant JAR.
  • Unused and undeclared dependencies: resolves the classes your sources name via the code index and reports dependencies that are used but only arrive transitively (also live on the import in the editor), declared ones that no source names, and compile dependencies only tests use – with one-click declare, remove or change scope. Known runtime-only libraries (JDBC drivers, logging backends, test engines) and JARs that register services are not reported as unused for sure.
  • Upgrade simulator: "what happens if I raise X to version Y?" – before the POM changes. Finds the place that sets the version today (property, BOM import, parent, direct declaration, dependencyManagement), applies the change in memory, rebuilds every module's dependency tree from the POMs and shows what goes up, down, appears, disappears or changes scope, plus new conflicts where a higher requested version loses. Missing POMs of the new version are fetched only on click; one more click applies exactly the simulated change.
  • Complements Maven Helper and the Dependency Analyzer: they show facts, Maven Detective shows cause and fix.
